According to the EFCC Chairman, the 146 foreigners would serve their jail terms before being repatriated to their country.
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has announced the conviction and sentencing of 146 out of 194 foreign nationals arrested in connection with cybersecurity-related financial crimes in Nigeria.
The statement was made by Mr. Ola Olukoyede, Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), on Wednesday at the Abuja Continental Hotel during the opening ceremony of the International Cybersecurity Conference.
The event was organised by the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA).
Attendees at the conference included the National Security Adviser, Malam Nuhu Ribadu; the Senate Committee Chairman on Cybersecurity, Senator Shuaibu Salihu; the Chairman of the House Committee on Cybersecurity, Mr. Stanley Adedeji; the United States Ambassador to Nigeria, Mr. Richards Mills; and the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Communications, Innovations, and Digital Economy, Mr. Adeladan Rafiu, among others.
According to the EFCC Chairman, the 146 foreigners would serve their jail terms before being repatriated to their country.
He praised the FBI, Interpol and other international security institutions for their support in ensuring successful prosecution of the cyber criminals.
Olukoyede said the EFCC would soon inaugurate a Cybersecurity Centre in its facility with the capability to detect and respond to Cybersecurity attacks within one hour, stressing that Cybersecurity attacks relating to financial crimes are becoming more organised across the world.
He said it had become imperative for security institutions and agencies as well as banks and regulatory bodies to collaborate to combat cyber crimes, saying the EFCC would soon Commission a 500-capacity Research Centre for reformation and rehabilitation of convicted cyber criminals.
“Last year, we arrested about 194 foreigners who were involved in various forms of financial crimes and activities that are inimical to the economic growth and development of our country.
“Today, I can tell you that we have succeeded in prosecution and conviction of 146 of them. They will serve their jail terms and will be repatriated to their respective countries, ” Olukoyede said.
This is coming a day after SaharaReporters reported that the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) stated that its operatives from the Kaduna Zonal Directorate arrested nine suspected illegal miners in Kaniyan Village, Mokwa Local Government Area, Niger State.
According to a statement released by the Commission on Tuesday, the arrest followed the receipt of actionable intelligence regarding ongoing illegal mining operations in the area.
The suspects include five Chinese nationals and four Nigerians.
The Chinese nationals were identified as Wu Ping, Xu XianLiang, Xu Aimin, Xeu Cihuo, and Liu Changhua, while the Nigerian suspects were identified as Ibrahim Abdullahi, Sunday Oladele, Destiny John, and Bulus Samuel.
Upon their arrest, EFCC operatives recovered a substantial cache of industrial mining and power equipment allegedly used in the illegal operation.

Muktasari:
- Silinde amewataka wadau wa kilimo kuongeza juhudi za kuwafikia vijana wengi zaidi katika maeneo ambayo imewekeza ya mashamba
Mbeya. Naibu Waziri wa Kilimo, David Silinde amesema Serikali itaendelea kushirikiana na wadau kuwekeza kwenye sekta ya kilimo kupitia miradi ya kimkakati chini ya Programu ya Kujenga Kesho iliyo Bora (BBT).
Pamoja na hayo, Silinde amewataka wadau wa kilimo kuongeza juhudi za kuwafikia vijana wengi zaidi katika maeneo ambayo imewekeza ya mashamba makubwa kwa ajili ya kutekeleza programu hiyo ya BBT.
Silinde ametoa kauli hiyo leo Jumanne, Septemba 17, 2024, alipokuwa akikabidhi vifaa kwa vijana 105 wanaojihusisha na kilimo kupitia mradi wa kuimarisha sekta binafsi unaotekelezwa na Kampuni ya Kibanza kwa ufadhili wa Shirika la Watu wa Marekani (USAID) katika wilaya za Mbeya, Mbarali na Chunya.
“Jitihada kubwa zinazofanywa na Serikali kwa kushirikiana na wadau wa sekta binafsi zimeleta mafanikio makubwa katika kuongeza thamani ya mazao, sambamba na ushiriki wa USAID kupitia mradi wa Feed the Future,” amesema Silinde.
Aidha, amewahamasisha vijana kutumia fursa zinazotolewa na sekta ya kilimo, akisisitiza kuwa mikoa ya Mbeya na Songwe imekuwa kitovu cha Wizara ya Kilimo katika uzalishaji wa mazao ya chakula na biashara.
“Serikali imewekeza katika mashamba makubwa kupitia mradi wa BBT, Wilaya ya Chunya, Mkoa wa Mbeya, imetenga hekari 57,000 kwa ajili ya kilimo,” amesema naibu waziri huyo.
Mkurugenzi Mtendaji wa Kampuni ya Kibanza, Jumanne Sanga amesema vijana 502 wamepewa mafunzo ya usindikaji wa bidhaa pamoja na elimu juu ya mabadiliko ya tabianchi na matumizi bora ya unyevu kwenye uzalishaji.
Amesema lengo ni kuwawezesha vijana kuongeza thamani ya mazao yao na kutumia mbinu mbalimbali za kukabiliana na changamoto za mabadiliko ya tabianchi.
Imeelezwa kuwa vijana 30,000 tayari wamefikiwa na mradi huo katika mikoa mbalimbali, ikiwamo Mbeya, Iringa na Morogoro, huku vijana 15,000 wakipata ajira. Aidha, vijana 3,000 wanatarajiwa kunufaika na mkopo wa Sh4.6 bilioni kupitia mradi wa Feed the Future ifikapo mwaka 2027.
Mnufaika wa mradi huo, Mariam Mkisi anayejishughulisha na usindikaji wa pilipili, amesema mradi huo umemsaidia kuunganishwa na masoko makubwa ya ndani na nje ya nchi kwa ajili ya usambazaji wa bidhaa zake.
a5410.en:
Summary:
- Silinde has asked agricultural stakeholders to increase efforts to reach more young people in the areas where it has invested in farms

Mbeya. The Deputy Minister of Agriculture, David Silinde, has said the Government will continue to work with stakeholders to invest in the agriculture sector through strategic projects under the Building a Better Tomorrow (BBT) Programme.

In addition, Silinde has asked agricultural stakeholders to increase efforts to reach more young people in the areas where large farms have been invested in for the implementation of the BBT programme.

Silinde made these remarks today, Tuesday, September 17, 2024, while handing over equipment to 105 young people engaged in agriculture through the private sector strengthening project implemented by Kibanza Company with funding from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) in the districts of Mbeya, Mbarali and Chunya.

"The great efforts being made by the Government in collaboration with private sector stakeholders have brought great success in adding value to crops, along with USAID's participation through the Feed the Future project," said Silinde.

He also encouraged young people to use the opportunities offered by the agriculture sector, stressing that the Mbeya and Songwe regions have been the centre of the Ministry of Agriculture in the production of food and cash crops.

"The Government has invested in large farms through the BBT project; Chunya District, Mbeya Region, has set aside 57,000 acres for agriculture," said the deputy minister.

The Executive Director of Kibanza Company, Jumanne Sanga, said 502 young people have been given training in product processing as well as education on climate change and the efficient use of moisture in production.

He said the aim is to enable young people to add value to their crops and to use various methods to cope with the challenges of climate change.

It was explained that 30,000 young people have already been reached by the project in various regions, including Mbeya, Iringa and Morogoro, with 15,000 young people getting employment. In addition, 3,000 young people are expected to benefit from a loan of 4.6 billion shillings through the Feed the Future project by 2027.

A beneficiary of the project, Mariam Mkisi, who is engaged in chilli processing, said the project has helped her to be connected to large domestic and foreign markets for the distribution of her products.

Liberia’s Public Works Minister has received public backlash for his absence at a commissioning ceremony for a bridge project to connect Liberia and Côte d’Ivoire.
By Patrick N. Mensah, Maryland County
Tuesday, October 8, 2024/Following Liberian officials’ conspicuous absence at the recent commissioning of a US$15M bridge project between Liberia and neighboring Côte d’Ivoire, several citizens in Maryland County are calling on Minister of Public Works Roland Giddings to explain why he wasn’t part of the joyful occasion attended by his Ivorian counterpart.
The ceremony was initiated by the ECOWAS Commission to construct a bridge over the Cavalla River that connects Liberia and Côte d’Ivoire.
The program took place at Plulo Border in Côte d’Ivoire on Thursday, October 3, 2024, without officials from Monrovia.
The ceremony was attended by representatives from ECOWAS, AIM LTD Engineer Michael Ihimekpen, Liary Tao SCEGC Project manager, the Ivorian government, and other regional stakeholders.
The ECOWAS Commission is collaborating with the African Development Bank to implement the bridge project, which is expected to benefit about 400 million people in the West African region.
Speaking on a local radio talk show in the county, many citizens, in anger, wondered whether the Government of Liberia, through the Ministry of Public Works, is concerned about Liberians’ safety and free movement.
According to them, such a great occasion that will bring relief to peoples of both countries attended by representatives from ECOWAS, SHAANXI Construction Engineering Corporation LTD, and Engineers from Côte d’Ivoire was held without the presence of Minister Giddings or any representative of the Ministry of Public Works.
However, the Public Works boss through ECOWAS Project Manager, Ashok Maliki, was contacted during the opening of the program why he had not arrived when his Ivorian counterparts were already present at the occasion, responded that he was stuck in the mud near Nimbia County in Liberia.
But the citizens termed Minister Giddings’s response embarrassing because they were looking forward to seeing him perform at the event, as it would’ve drawn the attention of ECOWAS and Chinese engineers gearing up for the project.
According to them, despite their excitement and anticipation, the Public Works Ministry was nowhere around, which they described as worrisome and questionable.
Pastor Abraham Togba, a resident of Zone 7A and one of the callers on the radio talk show, laments that the absence of Liberian officials at such a great occasion wasn’t only embarrassing but disgraceful to the entire country because President Boakai can’t be everywhere and that’s why he appointed cabinet ministers to fill such gap, but notes that to have heard the Minister saying he wasn’t present because his vehicle stuck in the mud, was a big shame.
Pastor Tobga adds that such an excuse was very poor, stressing that Giddings had been invited and informed about the event days before the ceremony.
“So the Minister who should’ve had the roads fixed is crying of being stuck; what happens to ordinary Liberians that use the roads on a daily basis?” He asks.
Pastor Togba continues that Liberians will now begin to notice the change they made in the poll, whether it’s positive or negative, adding that it’s so early for people to start criticizing the government for not attending important events.
Another caller from Zone 11, Mr. Jerryling Geetah, says, “I can’t believe that the Public Works Ministry or Minister didn’t show up. We have been praying tirelessly for years to make this event a success, and he couldn’t even spare a few hours to unbrace such a great occasion.” Mr. Geetah’s disappointment was felt emotionally.
He explains that there are reasons why such things are happening in Liberia, such as people’s unwillingness to correct wrongs. He also points out that even in the Minister’s absence, the County Resident Engineer should have shown up, pointing out that the program wasn’t held secretly or behind closed doors.
He believes that Liberian officials didn’t turn out only because ECOWAS did not bring money to share, noting that had that been the case, the entire place would’ve been filled with Liberian officials.
He calls on President Boakia to take such occasions seriously and take action against officials who downplay them because this could undermine his government’s growth and development.
“So to say, we are watching because we will not allow any government officials to stop our progress and developments. Other countries are moving forward, and we are still behind due to some officials’ attitudes,” Caller Geetah laments.
Also speaking, Mr. Jacob Towliad, a supporter of the ruling Unity Party and a public school teacher, criticizes the Public Works Minister’s absence. “I thought Minister Giddings would’ve come for sure because road connectivity has always been his involvement and activities. I can’t believe he has made such a statement.”
He maintains that, given the importance attached to the project, it was prudent that the Minister should’ve taken a flight to Maryland, as he claimed the roads were bad.
“Let me say, it was a failure on the part of the Minister and the local officials of the county because their presence was very important during such an occasion”, Mr. Towliad underscores.
Meanwhile, as the day went on, more and more people joined in the conversation, expressing their disappointment and disapproval of Mr. Giddings’ absence. Some even thought that the Minister was selfish and didn’t care about the people within the region.
However, The NEW DAWN observes that despite the absence of the Ministry of Public Works, local government officials within the county weren’t also seen doing the commissioning ceremony, which has drawn the attention of not only residents of Maryland but ECOWAS representatives at the program.
Notwithstanding, Director Appiah disclosed that official groundbreaking for the project will be done hopefully in November this year and is expected to bring together the Presidents of both countries when the Public Works Minister may attend.
The Acting Director of Transport of the ECOWAS Commission, Mr. Chris Appiah, says the bridge project is an ECOWAS Commission’s initiative through its President in collaboration with the African Development Bank as a way of giving back to 400 million people living within the West African region. Editing by Jonathan Browne

a5526.t:
Le 31 juillet 2025, grâce à la coopération étroite entre les gouvernements et les entreprises du Burundi et de la Chine, le premier lot de 38,4 tonnes de grains de café arabica burundais a été expédié avec succès vers la Chine. Il s’agit de la première exportation directe de grains de café burundais vers le marché chinois, marquant également un jalon important dans l’accès des produits burundais aux avantages du traitement de tarif douanier zéro à 100% des produits exportés vers la Chine. Par la suite, les entreprises des deux parties ont signé des contrats d’achat portant sur plus de 900 tonnes de grains de café burundais, pour une valeur totale de plus de 5 millions de dollars américains. Cela témoigne de la forte reconnaissance du marché chinois envers la qualité du café burundais et constitue une impulsion majeure pour le développement des exportations agricoles et de l’économie burundaise.
Depuis longtemps, le Burundi accorde une grande importance au développement de la filière café et s’engage à augmenter les revenus d’exportation du café. Désormais, grâce à la politique tarifaire préférentielle accordée par la Chine et à la fluidité des canaux de coopération sino-burundaise, le café burundais accède directement au deuxième plus grand marché de consommation au monde. Ce progrès constitue un véritable saut « du champ à la tasse ». Il permet non seulement de réduire considérablement les coûts douaniers et d’améliorer l’efficacité du marché, mais aussi de renforcer la durabilité et l’autonomie des exportations agricoles du Burundi.
Cette première expédition ne représente pas seulement un succès commercial, elle témoigne également de la mise en œuvre concrète des engagements de la Chine envers l’Afrique. La Chine reste toujours le partenaire de développement fiable du continent africain. Face à un contexte mondial marqué par l’incertitude, la Chine continue de promouvoir l’ouverture et la coopération gagnant-gagnant, et œuvrant à l’édification d’une communauté d’avenir partagé sino-africaine de haut niveau.
Depuis le 1er décembre 2024, la Chine a accordé le traitement de tarif douanier zéro à 100% des produits exportés vers la Chine par les pays les moins avancés, dont 33 pays africains. Elle est ainsi devenue le premier pays en développement et la première grande économie au monde à appliquer une telle mesure. En juin de 2025, la Chine a annoncé la mise en œuvre de la politique de tarif douanier zéro sur 100% des produits taxables pour les 53 pays africains ayant des relations diplomatiques avec elle. Cette politique ne se limite pas à une réduction tarifaire, elle représente un dividende de développement, une initiative pour le bien-être des populations et un modèle de coopération gagnant-gagnant. Elle vise à accompagner les pays africains dans le développement d’économies tournées vers l’exportation, à créer des emplois et à contribuer au bien-être de la population locale.
Comme le dit un proverbe chinois, « Il faut voir loin pour mieux avancer ». Cette année 2025 marque le 25e anniversaire de la création du Forum sur la coopération sino-africaine. L’exportation des premiers grains de café n’est qu’un début. À l’avenir, la Chine souhaite travailler main dans la main avec le Burundi pour promouvoir une coopération de haute qualité dans le cadre de l’Initiative « la Ceinture et la Route » et pour mettre en œuvre les « Dix actions de partenariat pour promouvoir conjointement la modernisation». Nous espérons que davantage de produits burundais de qualité entreront sur le marché chinois grâce à la politique de tarif douanier zéro. Nous invitons également les entreprises burundaises à saisir les opportunités offertes par l’exposition internationale d’importation de Chine, l’exposition économique et commerciale Chine-Afrique, ainsi que par les plateformes de commerce électronique de la Route de la soie, afin que les produits burundais puissent vraiment « entrer, rester et bien se vendre » en Chine, tout en partageant les fruits du développement chinois avec le peuple burundais.
D’un grain de café à la concrétisation d’une politique nationale, d’un carton de marchandises à l’ouverture d’une nouvelle ère de coopération mutuellement bénéfique, chaque pas de la coopération sino-burundaise témoigne de l’interaction sincère entre les peuples et de l’engagement ferme envers l’avenir. Les premiers pas du café burundais sur le marché chinois sont prometteurs, portés par un soutien politique solide, des dividendes de développement tangibles et de vastes perspectives de coopération. La Chine continuera à promouvoir activement une coopération économique et commerciale sino-burundaise de haute qualité, à soutenir l’entrée davantage de produits burundais sur son marché, et à ouvrir une nouvelle ère de coopération sino-burundaise plus prospère, mutuellement avantageuse et durable.
Ambassadeur de Chine au Burundi
Zhao Jiangping
a5526.en:
On 31 July 2025, thanks to close cooperation between the governments and enterprises of Burundi and China, the first batch of 38.4 tonnes of Burundian arabica coffee beans was successfully shipped to China. This is the first direct export of Burundian coffee beans to the Chinese market, and also marks an important milestone in Burundian products gaining access to the benefits of the zero-tariff treatment applied to 100% of products exported to China. Subsequently, enterprises on both sides signed purchase contracts covering more than 900 tonnes of Burundian coffee beans, for a total value of more than 5 million US dollars. This testifies to the strong recognition by the Chinese market of the quality of Burundian coffee and constitutes a major boost for the development of Burundi’s agricultural exports and economy.

For a long time now, Burundi has attached great importance to the development of the coffee sector and is committed to increasing coffee export revenues. Now, thanks to the preferential tariff policy granted by China and to the smoothness of Sino-Burundian cooperation channels, Burundian coffee gains direct access to the world’s second-largest consumer market. This progress constitutes a genuine leap “from the field to the cup”. It not only makes it possible to reduce customs costs considerably and improve market efficiency, but also to strengthen the sustainability and autonomy of Burundi’s agricultural exports.

This first shipment does not represent only a commercial success; it also testifies to the concrete implementation of China’s commitments towards Africa. China always remains the African continent’s reliable development partner. Faced with a global context marked by uncertainty, China continues to promote openness and win-win cooperation, and works towards building a high-level China-Africa community of shared future.

Since 1 December 2024, China has granted zero-tariff treatment to 100% of the products exported to China by the least developed countries, including 33 African countries. It thus became the first developing country and the first major economy in the world to apply such a measure. In June 2025, China announced the implementation of the zero-tariff policy on 100% of taxable products for the 53 African countries having diplomatic relations with it. This policy is not limited to a tariff reduction; it represents a development dividend, an initiative for the well-being of populations and a model of win-win cooperation. It aims to support African countries in developing export-oriented economies, to create jobs and to contribute to the well-being of the local population.

As a Chinese proverb says, “One must look far ahead in order to advance better.” This year, 2025, marks the 25th anniversary of the creation of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation. The export of the first coffee beans is only a beginning. In future, China wishes to work hand in hand with Burundi to promote high-quality cooperation within the framework of the Belt and Road Initiative and to implement the “Ten partnership actions for jointly promoting modernisation”. We hope that more quality Burundian products will enter the Chinese market thanks to the zero-tariff policy. We also invite Burundian enterprises to seize the opportunities offered by the China International Import Expo, the China-Africa Economic and Trade Expo, as well as by the Silk Road e-commerce platforms, so that Burundian products can truly “enter, remain and sell well” in China, while sharing the fruits of Chinese development with the Burundian people.

From a coffee bean to the realisation of a national policy, from a carton of goods to the opening of a new era of mutually beneficial cooperation, every step of Sino-Burundian cooperation testifies to the sincere interaction between the peoples and to the firm commitment to the future. Burundian coffee’s first steps on the Chinese market are promising, carried by solid political support, tangible development dividends and vast prospects for cooperation. China will continue actively to promote high-quality Sino-Burundian economic and trade cooperation, to support the entry of more Burundian products onto its market, and to open a new era of more prosperous, mutually advantageous and sustainable Sino-Burundian cooperation.

Ambassador of China to Burundi
Zhao Jiangping

a5592.t:
Economic analysts have expressed fears that the temporary ban on foreign imposed by the US government could worsen the forex shortages the country is experiencing in the short to medium term.
The concerns follow an announcement from the US government that President Donald Trump’s administration has paused all foreign assistance funded by or through the State Department and United States Agency for International Development pending review.
The move will reportedly cost Malawi about $284.7 million in foreign aid.
Catholic University economics lecturer Greenson Nyirenda said the loss could worsen the country’s forex crisis.
“The funding by international organisations remains one of the significant sources of forex for countries like Malawi that have low exportation capacity. This will hit hard,” he said.
Echoing Nyirenda’s sentiments, Scotland-based Malawian economist Velli Nyirongo warned that the reduced forex availability could strain reserves, weaken the government’s ability to meet external obligations, and destabilise the exchange rate.
“Over time, sustained aid withdrawal may exacerbate fiscal imbalances, forcing the government to seek alternative financing through increased borrowing or expanded export earnings, both of which may take time to materialise,” he said in a WhatsApp response.
Nyirongo further said policy makers may need to tighten monetary policy, diversify export earning, strengthen remittance inflows, and secure alternative funding from multilateral institutions or regional trade agreements.
Figures from the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) show that total forex reserves in November had dropped to $516.9 million (2.1 months of imports) at the end of November 2024, far below the 3.9 months of import cover recommended by multilateral institutions such as the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
This is also lower than the $568.9 million (equivalent to 2.3 months of imports) recorded in November 2023, when the government devalued the kwacha by 44 percent as part of a broader set of reforms to restore macroeconomic stability.
The analysts observed that the pause, if prolonged, could deepen economic instability.
In December last year, the government introduced a new set of forex controls that would require public institutions, including research institutions and public universities with donor-funded projects to open foreign-denominated accounts at RBM.
They will also be required to convert 80 percent of their foreign currency receipts into Malawi kwacha, and non-governmental organisations will be required to convert 70 percent of their forex receipts into the local currency.
The move split opinion with one section of economic analysts saying it would help contain the parallel forex market. In contrast, another section said it would incentivise traders to use the black market.

a5637.t:
L’actualité nord-africaine de ce vendredi met en lumière l’activisme diplomatique du Maroc autour de l’Initiative atlantique, les tensions croissantes entre Paris et Alger, des tendances économiques contrastées en Tunisie et en Algérie, ainsi que des dynamiques de coopération régionales en Libye et en Égypte.
En ouverture, la diplomatie marocaine s’est illustrée à Awaza, au Turkménistan, où l’ambassadeur Omar Hilale a rappelé, selon Al Ahdath Al Maghribia, que sous l’impulsion du Roi Mohammed VI, Rabat soutient activement les pays africains sans littoral via des projets Sud-Sud et triangulaires destinés à favoriser l’intégration régionale et les investissements. Cette vision a trouvé un écho positif auprès du Burkina Faso où le ministre des Affaires étrangères, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, a salué, dans les colonnes de Rissalat Al Oumma, cette initiative comme une source d’inspiration pour l’accès des États du Sahel à l’Atlantique.
Sur le plan stratégique, Libération rapporte que le président américain Donald Trump a réaffirmé la reconnaissance par Washington de la souveraineté marocaine sur le Sahara, que le journaliste péruvien Ricardo Sanchez Serra décrit comme une « alliance historique » entre Rabat et Washington.
Côté humanitaire, Al Ittihad Al Ichtiraki souligne que le ministre palestinien Ahmed Assaf a salué l’aide humanitaire et médicale envoyée par le Roi Mohammed VI à Gaza, insistant sur son impact direct pour la population.
Enfin, sur le front économique, Annahar Al Maghribia relève que les régimes marocains de retraite ont collecté 66,8 milliards de dirhams en 2024 (+8,9 %), versant 71,1 milliards de prestations, avec des réserves proches de 327 milliards.
En transition, la relation entre Paris et Alger s’est encore tendue : TSA rapporte qu’après la suspension par la France des exemptions de visa, Alger a dénoncé toute forme de pression et annoncé des mesures de réciprocité touchant les visas et les biens immobiliers. Sur le plan économique et régional, L’Expression fait savoir que la Communauté d’Afrique de l’Est a lancé l’« EAC Bond », un mécanisme de caution douanière unique censé fluidifier le commerce intra-africain, et perçu comme un outil renforçant l’intégration. Par ailleurs, APS indique que l’Algérie a lancé un appel aux compétences nationales et à sa diaspora pour créer un conseil d’expertises dédié au développement d’une industrie mécanique intégrée.
En matière économique, La Presse annonce que les investissements déclarés en Tunisie ont progressé de 16,9 % sur six mois, atteignant 3,3 milliards de dinars tunisiens, soutenus par un projet touristique de 300 millions de dinars à Jendouba. Cependant, Tunisie Numérique relève que la demande intérieure s’effondre, ne tenant que grâce aux transferts des Tunisiens de l’étranger, dans un contexte de flambée des prix. Sur le plan judiciaire, La Presse signale la remise en liberté du directeur régional de la Sûreté nationale de Nabeul après une semaine de détention dans le cadre d’une enquête.
La coopération régionale reste au cœur de l’agenda libyen : eanlibya.com rapporte que Tripoli et Alger discutent du renforcement des relations bilatérales dans divers domaines, avec un accent sur des dossiers régionaux d’intérêt commun. Le même média indique que la Libye et l’ONU se sont accordées sur des partenariats pour la mise en œuvre des Objectifs de développement durable, incluant l’inclusion financière et la résilience environnementale. Dans le domaine sécuritaire, eanlibya.com précise que des militaires libyens ont pris part à l’exercice « Africa Peace 3 » organisé par l’Algérie pour améliorer les capacités de maintien de la paix. Enfin, gomhuriaonline signale la signature d’un protocole entre les ministères libyens des Transports et des Habous pour promouvoir la sécurité routière et les valeurs civiques.
En clôture de cette revue, egyptindependent rapporte que Donald Trump a imposé un droit de douane de 10 % sur les importations égyptiennes, touchant cinq catégories majeures d’exportations, une mesure susceptible d’impacter directement les équilibres commerciaux du Caire.
MK/ac/Sf/APA
a5637.en:
This Friday's North African news highlights Morocco's diplomatic activism around the Atlantic Initiative, growing tensions between Paris and Algiers, contrasting economic trends in Tunisia and Algeria, as well as regional cooperation dynamics in Libya and Egypt.

To open, Moroccan diplomacy distinguished itself in Awaza, Turkmenistan, where Ambassador Omar Hilale recalled, according to Al Ahdath Al Maghribia, that under the impetus of King Mohammed VI, Rabat actively supports landlocked African countries through South-South and triangular projects intended to promote regional integration and investment. This vision found a positive echo in Burkina Faso, where the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Karamoko Jean Marie Traore, welcomed, in the columns of Rissalat Al Oumma, this initiative as a source of inspiration for Sahel states' access to the Atlantic.

On the strategic front, Liberation reports that American President Donald Trump reaffirmed Washington's recognition of Moroccan sovereignty over the Sahara, which Peruvian journalist Ricardo Sanchez Serra describes as a "historic alliance" between Rabat and Washington.

On the humanitarian side, Al Ittihad Al Ichtiraki underlines that Palestinian minister Ahmed Assaf welcomed the humanitarian and medical aid sent by King Mohammed VI to Gaza, insisting on its direct impact on the population.

Finally, on the economic front, Annahar Al Maghribia notes that Moroccan pension schemes collected 66.8 billion dirhams in 2024 (+8.9%), paying out 71.1 billion in benefits, with reserves close to 327 billion.

In transition, the relationship between Paris and Algiers has become further strained: TSA reports that after France suspended visa exemptions, Algiers denounced any form of pressure and announced reciprocal measures affecting visas and real estate. On the economic and regional front, L'Expression reports that the East African Community has launched the "EAC Bond," a single customs bond mechanism meant to smooth intra-African trade, and perceived as a tool strengthening integration. In addition, APS indicates that Algeria has issued a call to national talent and to its diaspora to create an expertise council dedicated to developing an integrated mechanical industry.

In economic matters, La Presse announces that declared investments in Tunisia rose by 16.9% over six months, reaching 3.3 billion Tunisian dinars, supported by a 300-million-dinar tourism project in Jendouba. However, Tunisie Numerique notes that domestic demand is collapsing, holding up only thanks to transfers from Tunisians abroad, in a context of soaring prices. On the judicial front, La Presse reports the release of the regional director of National Security of Nabeul after a week in detention as part of an investigation.

Regional cooperation remains at the heart of the Libyan agenda: eanlibya.com reports that Tripoli and Algiers are discussing the strengthening of bilateral relations in various fields, with an emphasis on regional matters of common interest. The same outlet indicates that Libya and the UN have agreed on partnerships for the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals, including financial inclusion and environmental resilience. In the security field, eanlibya.com specifies that Libyan soldiers took part in the "Africa Peace 3" exercise organised by Algeria to improve peacekeeping capacities. Finally, gomhuriaonline reports the signing of a protocol between the Libyan ministries of Transport and Religious Endowments (Habous) to promote road safety and civic values.

Closing this review, egyptindependent reports that Donald Trump has imposed a 10% customs duty on Egyptian imports, affecting five major categories of exports, a measure likely to directly impact Cairo's trade balances.

O ministro do Comércio, Indústria e Energia, Alexandre Monteiro, afirmou esta sexta-feira, em conferência de imprensa, que o Governo está a trabalhar para restabelecer o fornecimento normal de electricidade em Santiago, mas sem se comprometer com prazos concretos.
Projectos do acordo de troca de dívida de Cabo Verde com Portugal estão a avançar - ministro
O ministro da Energia, Alexandre Monteiro, disse à Lusa que os projectos no âmbito do acordo de troca de dívida por investimentos climáticos com Portugal estão a avançar, salientando que já foi criado legalmente o fundo climático e ambiental.
Cabo Verde espera poupar quase o dobro em combustíveis com aumento de renováveis
Estimativa do ministro da Energia. Em 2023, país economizou quase 2 milhões de contos. Governante diz ainda que Cabo Verde quer alcançar 100% de acesso à electricidade até 2026
"Ajuda a Gaza? Nenhum interruptor será ligado até que raptados regressem"
O ministro da Energia de Israel, Israel Katz, advertiu hoje que o seu país não permitirá a entrada de bens essenciais ou ajuda humanitária em Gaza até que o Hamas liberte as pessoas sequestradas no sábado em Israel.
“Projectos já ultrapassam os 30% de penetração de energias renováveis previstos para 2026”
Governo conseguiu financiamento para projectos integrados no Programa Nacional de Sustentabilidade Energética. Um deles, a estação de pump and storage que vai ser construída no concelho da Ribeira Grande de Santiago, está orçado em cerca de 70 milhões de euros. Investimentos feitos na área das energias renováveis e da transição energética vão permitir uma redução de 22% no consumo de combustíveis fósseis na produção de electricidade, assegura o ministro da Energia, Alexandre Monteiro, que anuncia igualmente que o governo está a estudar a possibilidade de aumentar os incentivos na compra de táxis com motor eléctrico.
Preço do gás e do fuel para produção de electricidade congelados, gasolina e gasóleo com aumento máximo de 5%
Ministros da Energia anunciou hoje, em conferência de imprensa, as medidas de mitigação da subida de preços dos combustíveis.
Governo quer estar preparado para “mitigar a situação”
Guerra na Ucrânia faz disparar preços do petróleo nos mercados internacionais. Governo garante que está a acompanhar a situação e que vai avaliar “instrumentos disponíveis” para diminuir os impactos que a subida do preço do petróleo nos mercados internacionais terá em Cabo Verde.
COVID-19: Governo reúne-se com empresas do sector energético
Ministro da energia e empresas do sector energético estiveram reunidos, hoje de manhã, para analisar os impactos provocados pela pandemia de COVID-19 no sector energético nacional. Retoma no sector dos combustíveis e electricidade será feita à medida que o consumo volte ao normal, assegura o ministro.
Assistência técnica do Banco Mundial para privatização da Electra arranca este mês
O ministro da Indústria, Comércio e Energia garantiu que arranca este mês a assistência técnica do Banco Mundial (BM) com vista à privatização da empresa de produção de água e energia (Electra).
Processo de privatização da Electra "está a decorrer normalmente" -Ministro da Energia
O ministro da Indústria, Comércio e Energia disse esta quarta-feira que a privatização da Electra não vai ser este ano, mas admitiu que se está a elaborar o trabalho técnico de suporte para ser apresentado ao Governo.
Alexandre Monteiro, ministro da Energia: Micro-geração está a crescer e é “aposta acertada”
Um ano depois do início da implementação do novo plano energético pelo governo, Alexandre Monteiro faz um balanço do que foi feito e do que se perspectiva para o futuro.

Articles about the Minister of Energy

Blackouts leave patients in the middle of examinations in Praia
For about a month and a half the Cabo Verdean capital has been living between the sound of generators and the darkness of successive power cuts, interrupting medical examinations and delaying production at small and medium-sized enterprises, the backbone of the economy.

“We are not committing to dates” for the resolution of the energy problems – Minister of Energy
The Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy, Alexandre Monteiro, stated this Friday, at a press conference, that the Government is working to restore the normal supply of electricity in Santiago, but without committing to concrete deadlines.

Projects under Cabo Verde’s debt swap agreement with Portugal are advancing – minister
The Minister of Energy, Alexandre Monteiro, told Lusa that the projects under the debt-for-climate-investment swap agreement with Portugal are advancing, stressing that the climate and environment fund has already been legally created.

Cabo Verde expects to save almost double on fuels with the increase in renewables
Estimate by the Minister of Energy. In 2023 the country saved almost 2 million contos. The official also says that Cabo Verde wants to achieve 100% access to electricity by 2026.

“Aid to Gaza? No switch will be turned on until the kidnapped return”
Israel’s Minister of Energy, Israel Katz, warned today that his country will not allow the entry of essential goods or humanitarian aid into Gaza until Hamas releases the people kidnapped on Saturday in Israel.

“Projects already exceed the 30% penetration of renewable energy foreseen for 2026”
The Government has obtained financing for projects integrated into the National Energy Sustainability Programme. One of them, the pump-and-storage station that will be built in the municipality of Ribeira Grande de Santiago, is budgeted at around 70 million euros. Investments made in the area of renewable energy and the energy transition will allow a 22% reduction in the consumption of fossil fuels in electricity production, assures the Minister of Energy, Alexandre Monteiro, who also announces that the government is studying the possibility of increasing incentives for the purchase of taxis with electric motors.

Price of gas and fuel for electricity production frozen, petrol and diesel with a maximum increase of 5%
The Minister of Energy announced today, at a press conference, the measures to mitigate the rise in fuel prices.

The war in Ukraine sends oil prices soaring on international markets. The Government guarantees that it is monitoring the situation and that it will assess the “available instruments” to reduce the impacts that the rise in the price of oil on international markets will have in Cabo Verde.

COVID-19: Government meets with companies in the energy sector
The Minister of Energy and companies in the energy sector met this morning to analyse the impacts caused by the COVID-19 pandemic on the national energy sector. Recovery in the fuel and electricity sector will take place as consumption returns to normal, the minister assures.

World Bank technical assistance for the privatisation of Electra starts this month
The Minister of Industry, Commerce and Energy guaranteed that the World Bank technical assistance with a view to the privatisation of the water and power production company (Electra) starts this month.

Electra privatisation process “is proceeding normally” – Minister of Energy
The Minister of Industry, Commerce and Energy said this Wednesday that the privatisation of Electra will not take place this year, but admitted that the technical support work is being prepared to be presented to the Government.

Alexandre Monteiro, Minister of Energy: Micro-generation is growing and is “the right bet”

Emmanuel Macron a affirmé avoir dit ce mardi 15 avril au Premier ministre israélien Benjamin Netanyahu que "le calvaire" des civils de Gaza devait "prendre fin", appelant à un cessez-le-feu permettant la libération des otages du Hamas et à "l'ouverture de tous les points de passage de l'aide humanitaire".
"Cessez-le-feu, libération de tous les otages, aide humanitaire, puis réouverture enfin d'une perspective de solution politique à deux États. C'est dans ce contexte que j'envisage la Conférence de juin" que la France coprésidera à l'ONU, "en prenant en compte les intérêts de sécurité d'Israël et de tous dans la région", a déclaré le président français sur le réseau X.
"Le calvaire que vivent les populations civiles de Gaza doit prendre fin", a-t-il demandé.
Avant d'ajouter: "L’ouverture de tous les points de passage de l’aide humanitaire est une nécessité vitale pour les populations civiles de Gaza. Je l’ai vu à El-Arish, cette aide est bloquée de l’autre côté de la frontière. Elle doit parvenir aux civils le plus vite possible".
"Une énorme récompense pour le terrorisme"
Emmanuel Macron a également répété que "le cessez-le-feu est la seule façon d’assurer la libération des otages toujours retenus par le Hamas".
"La libération de tous les otages a toujours été une priorité absolue, tout comme la démilitarisation du Hamas", a assuré le président français.
De son côté, Benjamin Netanyahu a déclaré à Emmanuel Macron que l'établissement d'un État palestinien serait "une énorme récompense pour le terrorisme", ont indiqué ses services.
"Au cours de la conversation, le Premier ministre s'est fermement opposé à la création d'un État palestinien, affirmant que cela constituerait une énorme récompense pour le terrorisme", a indiqué le bureau de Benjamin Netanyahu dans un communiqué.

a6022.en:
Emmanuel Macron said he told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday 15 April that "the ordeal" of Gaza's civilians must "come to an end", calling for a ceasefire that would allow the release of the Hamas hostages and for "the opening of all humanitarian aid crossing points".
"Ceasefire, release of all hostages, humanitarian aid, then finally the reopening of a prospect of a political two-State solution. It is in this context that I envisage the June Conference," which France will co-chair at the UN, "taking into account the security interests of Israel and of everyone in the region," the French president declared on the social network X.
"The ordeal being endured by the civilian populations of Gaza must come to an end," he demanded.
Before adding: "The opening of all humanitarian aid crossing points is a vital necessity for the civilian populations of Gaza. I saw it at El-Arish: this aid is blocked on the other side of the border. It must reach civilians as quickly as possible."
"An enormous reward for terrorism"
Emmanuel Macron also repeated that "the ceasefire is the only way to ensure the release of the hostages still held by Hamas".
"The release of all hostages has always been an absolute priority, as has the demilitarisation of Hamas," the French president affirmed.
For his part, Benjamin Netanyahu told Emmanuel Macron that the establishment of a Palestinian State would be "an enormous reward for terrorism", his office said.
"During the conversation, the Prime Minister firmly opposed the creation of a Palestinian State, saying that it would constitute an enormous reward for terrorism," Benjamin Netanyahu's office said in a statement.
Source: BFMTV.com...

Niamey, 20 Août (ANP) – Le lundi 19 août 2024 s’est tenue au Centre International de conférence Mahatma Gandhi de Niamey, la cérémonie de célébration de la Journée mondiale de l’aide humanitaire avec comme thème, ‘’Agir pour l’humanité’’.
La ministre de l’Action Humanitaire et de la Gestion des Catastrophes Mme Aïssa Laouan Wandarama qui a lancé officielle la cérémonie au nom du gouvernement, a rendu hommage ‘’au courage de ceux qui risquent leurs vies pour aider les plus démunis’’. C’est aussi une occasion de mettre en lumière, la résilience et surtout la générosité des communautés locales, qui en temps de crise, sont les premières à apporter secours aux personnes en détresse. ‘’Ces communautés méritent le respect et la considération de toute la communauté humanitaire, et doivent à ce titre être célébrées’’ selon elle.
Instituée par l’Assemblée générale des Nations Unies en 2008 pour honorer la mémoire des travailleurs humanitaires victimes de l’attentat contre la maison des Nations Unies le 19 août 2003 à Bagdad en Iraq, cette journée vise à rappeler au monde entier, que l’humanité est confrontée à une menace existentielle en raison de la violence qui caractérise les conflits.
Pour le compte de l’ONG Internationale Pathfinder, Harouna Zakou, Directeur pays Adjoint de Pathfinder International au Niger, a dans son adresse déclaré je cite « je voudrai profiter pour me joindre à l’ensemble de la grande famille humanitaire pour célébrer le courage, la détermination et l’engagement de tous les acteurs qui se battent au quotidien pour apporter des changements positifs dans la vie des communautés nigériennes aux côtés des autorités nationales ».
« Nous rendons hommage à tous les acteurs humanitaires qui se battent au quotidien pour que les populations les plus vulnérables puissent bénéficier des services sociaux de base et améliorer leurs conditions de vie. Rendre aussi hommage à tous ce qui bravent au jour le jour, les difficultés sur le terrain, les risques multiples auxquels ils sont exposés. Nous sommes dans la saison pluvieuse, avec des routes qui sont coupées, mais malgré cela il y a des hommes et des femmes qui se battent avec détermination pour apporter les services des soins de santé, de soutien économique et de subsistance aux populations vulnérables qui sont affectées par les fléaux et les difficultés de la vie. Nous disons bravo à ces acteurs et félicitations pour leur engagement ».
« Pathfinder, en tant que membre de cette grande famille humanitaire et du développement, travaille aux côtés du gouvernement et des autorités nigériennes depuis plus de 10 ans pour offrir l’accès aux soins de santé primaire, aux services de santé maternelle, néonatale et infantile, aux services de santé reproductive et de planification familiale de qualité, aux femmes et aux jeunes du Niger » fin de citation.
Harouna Zakou, a également salué et à féliciter tous les ‘’Pathfinders’’ au Niger et dans le monde entier qui sont engagées au jour le jour pour aller au-delà des barrières, et fournir des services de soin de santé essentiels aux populations les plus démunies au Niger et partout ailleurs dans le monde.
Pour terminer son allocution, le directeur Pays Adjoint de Pathfinder International au Niger a renouvelé l’engagement de l’organisation Internationale, à poursuivre les activités et le soutien au gouvernement du Niger pour renforcer la résilience des femmes, des jeunes et des populations les plus vulnérables au Niger.
Pathfinder a pour mission d’établir des partenariats locaux durables et de confiance pour renforcer les systèmes de santé, en forgeant des voies résilientes vers la santé et des droits sexuels et reproductifs pour toutes et tous. Parmi les projets de Pathfinder, il y a le J-Matassa qui est une nouvelle initiative en droits en santé sexuelle et reproductive (DSSR) visant les jeunes et les femmes dans le but de réduire les mariages précoces, les grossesses non désirées et la mortalité maternelle. Le projet offre ainsi plus d’opportunités aux adolescents et aux jeunes de poursuivre leurs études et apprentissage, afin de compléter leur développement personnel et professionnel, ainsi que leur autonomie financière pour briser le cycle vicieux de reproduction et de pauvreté et réaliser leur plein potentiel, et choisir leur propre voie.
SML/ANP/095/Août 2024
a6024.en:
Niamey, 20 August (ANP) - On Monday 19 August 2024, the ceremony marking World Humanitarian Day was held at the Mahatma Gandhi International Conference Centre in Niamey, under the theme "Act for Humanity".
The Minister of Humanitarian Action and Disaster Management, Mrs Aissa Laouan Wandarama, who officially launched the ceremony on behalf of the government, paid tribute "to the courage of those who risk their lives to help the most destitute". It is also an opportunity to highlight the resilience and above all the generosity of local communities, which in times of crisis are the first to bring relief to people in distress. "These communities deserve the respect and consideration of the entire humanitarian community, and must for that reason be celebrated," she said.
Established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2008 to honour the memory of the humanitarian workers killed in the attack on the United Nations house on 19 August 2003 in Baghdad, Iraq, this day aims to remind the whole world that humanity faces an existential threat because of the violence that characterises conflicts.
On behalf of the international NGO Pathfinder, Harouna Zakou, Deputy Country Director of Pathfinder International in Niger, declared in his address, and I quote: "I would like to take this opportunity to join the entire great humanitarian family in celebrating the courage, the determination and the commitment of all the actors who fight every day to bring positive changes to the lives of Nigerien communities alongside the national authorities."
"We pay tribute to all the humanitarian actors who fight every day so that the most vulnerable populations can benefit from basic social services and improve their living conditions. We also pay tribute to all those who brave, day after day, the difficulties in the field and the many risks to which they are exposed. We are in the rainy season, with roads that are cut off, but despite this there are men and women who fight with determination to bring health care services, economic and livelihood support to the vulnerable populations affected by the scourges and difficulties of life. We say bravo to these actors and congratulate them on their commitment."
"Pathfinder, as a member of this great humanitarian and development family, has been working alongside the government and the Nigerien authorities for more than 10 years to provide access to primary health care, to maternal, newborn and child health services, and to quality reproductive health and family planning services, for the women and young people of Niger." End of quote.
Harouna Zakou also saluted and congratulated all the "Pathfinders" in Niger and around the world who are committed day after day to going beyond barriers and providing essential health care services to the most destitute populations in Niger and everywhere else in the world.
To conclude his address, the Deputy Country Director of Pathfinder International in Niger renewed the international organisation's commitment to continuing its activities and its support to the government of Niger in order to strengthen the resilience of women, young people and the most vulnerable populations in Niger.
Pathfinder's mission is to build sustainable and trusted local partnerships to strengthen health systems, forging resilient pathways to sexual and reproductive health and rights for all. Among Pathfinder's projects is J-Matassa, a new initiative in sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) aimed at young people and women with the goal of reducing early marriage, unwanted pregnancies and maternal mortality. The project thus offers more opportunities to adolescents and young people to pursue their studies and training, in order to complete their personal and professional development, as well as their financial autonomy, so as to break the vicious cycle of reproduction and poverty, realise their full potential, and choose their own path.
SML/ANP/095/August 2024

The vast majority of the US Agency for International Development's (USAID) programmes have been terminated after a six-week purge, Secretary of State Marco Rubio has announced.
On X, Rubio said that the initiatives "spent tens of billions in ways that did not serve" or harmed US interests.
The remaining programmes - just 18% - will now be administered by the State Department.
Humanitarian organisations around the world have warned that the controversial move to end long-running US aid programmes is already having dire consequences around the world, potentially endangering lives.
The Trump administration has repeatedly made clear that it wants overseas spending to be closely aligned with its "America First" approach.
Shortly after Trump returned to the White House on 20 January, thousands of USAID employees were put on leave, and those working overseas recalled.
In an executive order signed on his first day, Trump also moved to freeze foreign assistance funding and ordered a review of USAID's work abroad, led by Elon Musk and the Department of Government Efficiency, or Doge.
Thousands of development contracts also were cancelled, and thousands of employees ultimately fired.
In his X post, Rubio said that after the review, the US was "officially ending" about 5,200 of USAID's 6,200 programmes.
"In consultation with Congress, we intend for the remaining 18% of programmes we are keeping....to be administered more effectively under the State Department," Rubio added.
Additionally, Rubio thanked Doge and State Department staff "who worked very long hours to achieve this overdue and historic reform".
Democrats and various humanitarian organisations have characterised the shutdown of USAID's programmes - which were funded by Congress - as illegal, prompting several lawsuits.
USAID was tasked with a wide variety of missions around the globe, ranging from famine detection to polio vaccinations and emergency food kitchens in conflict zones.
The freezes in funding and elimination of programmes is already having an impact.
In Sudan, for example, the freeze in humanitarian assistance has led to the shuttering of over 1,100 communal kitchens set up to help those left destitute by the country's ongoing civil war.
It is estimated that almost two million people have been affected.
In Oman, dozens of Afghan women who fled the Taliban government to pursue higher education now face return after their USAID-funded scholarships were abruptly terminated.
In another example, India's first medical clinic for transgender people shut operations in three cities after US President Donald Trump stopped foreign aid to it.

a6104.t:
By Women’s Land and Resource Rights (WLR²) Platform
“One woman or girl is killed every 10 minutes”
 United Nations 2024.
This is an alarming reminder of the escalating global crisis of gender-based violence (GBV). In Zambia, GBV cases surged by 28% in 2023, with 42,965 incidents reported. The Natural Resource Management (NRM) sector, deeply rooted in rural areas, remains particularly vulnerable to GBV due to entrenched social norms that perpetuate gender inequalities and violence. These norms restrict women’s decision-making, limit access to resources, and expose them to abuse, including economic and physical violence. Women also face limited job opportunities in male-dominated sectors, burdened by family responsibilities and insufficient spousal or family support. During the 2024 16 Days of Activism Against GBV, the Women’s Land and Resource Rights (WLR²) Platform urges greater attention and action to address GBV in Zambia’s NRM sectors.
Traditional and systemic barriers, including cultural norms, discriminatory policies, and unequal access to resources exacerbate gender-based violence in Zambia’s NRM sector. These barriers disproportionately affect women and girls, limiting their participation in and benefits from NRM while increasing their vulnerability to GBV. Despite the supportive legal & policy framework for promoting gender equality in Zambia, such as the 2011 Anti-Gender Based Violence Act, the 2015 Gender Equity and Equality Act and the 50-50 land allocation policy, only 22% of women are estimated to own land under state tenure. Most of the customary land is controlled by male-dominated traditional leadership systems. In fisheries, women are often coerced into exchanging sexual favors for access to fish, a practice known as “sex-for-fish,” which is common in Western Province and other regions. Similarly, with a representation of only 10% in community governance and 17%, community scouts’ women in wildlife law enforcement, face threats, including violence from poachers and workplace harassment. This stems from deeply ingrained power imbalances and economic dependence between men and women working in the NRM.
Established in 2023, the WLR² Platform aims to address women’s challenges and promote their role in NRM management in Zambia. Supported by USAID Integrated Land and Resource Governance II (ILRG II) the platform works with over 100 trained champions, to empower women and promote gender-responsive approaches. This is aimed at increasing women’s representation and access benefits in land and natural resource management. Between 2020 and 2022, ILRG worked with 25 government, civil society organizations (CSO’s), and private organizations to provide tools and capacity building to advance gender equality and address GBV in NRM. This support from USAID ILRG II program and The Nature Conservancy (TNC), will unite to officially launch the WLR² platform with the aim to continue empowering women in land NRM and promoting their rights.
The platform is actively raising awareness and supporting advocacy on the rights of women and girls in NRM sector as part of the commemoration of the 16 Days of Activism Against GBV, emphasizing its link to land and resource rights. The 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence is an annual global campaign running from November 25 to December 10. It is aimed at raising awareness and promoting action against violence targeting women and girls. The campaign spans over several key dates, 25 November (International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women), 29 November (International Women Human Rights Defenders Day), 1 December (World AIDS Day), 3 December (International Day for the Disabled), and 10 December (International Human Rights Day). As part of this global movement, WLR² will amplify voices, and challenge systemic barriers, as part of their long-term drive to meaningful change for women’s empowerment and safety in NRM.
Many gender and women’s rights champions have already shared their messages as part of the WLR² Platform 16 Days of Activism. Voices from the field include Samantha Munang’andu, RISE Project Coordinator at Action Aid Zambia, Maina Malaya, WCP Communications Officer and Monje Sabela Siyeni, Women’s Land and Resource Rights Platform Coordinator. The champions shared their challenges, success and commitments to fighting GBV in NRM and had the following to say.
“GBV is not just physical. It affects every aspect of a woman’s life, lowering her self-esteem, hampering her performance in leadership roles, and denying her economic opportunities. By championing the rights of women, I shine light on the critical need for GBV prevention in the fisheries sector.” Samantha Munang’andu, Action Aid
“Zambia’s wildlife management has made strides in addressing GBV by increasing women’s participation in roles like community scouts and conservation leaders. However, cultural resistance and limited access to leadership positions hinder progress and perpetuate GBV risks. During these 16 days of activism, I recommit to creating safe spaces for women, equipping them to excel in their roles, and fostering understanding among men to support women as indispensable allies” Maina Malaya, Wildlife Crime Prevention
“Gender based violence affects both women and men, but when GBV is related to land, it’s about the livelihoods of majority Zambians women and their children. Land belongs to men, they have the power, but women lack the power to own and combined with discriminatory rules and harmful social and gender norms, at the risk of experiencing gender-based violence heightened. They are denied inheritance rights, evicted from their land, threatened, or have land forcibly taken away. They stay in abusive relationships to have access to land and often experience sexual violence that is also used as a means of control over the land resource. Am standing up for women!” Monje Sabela Siyeni, WLR² Platform
Their words resonate with many women who continue to fight against systemic violence while championing sustainable natural resource management practices. This year’s 16 Days of Activism Against GBV campaign marks the Platform’s inaugural engagement with the NRM sector, aiming to highlight GBV issues and foster collaboration among organizations to share experiences. Women’s rights champions and allies are invited to share their GBV stories and the challenges of addressing it within the sector. These narratives will amplify survivors’ voices, inspire advocates, and drive collective action toward a more inclusive and equitable future. Share your story and be part of the change. With Zambia’s abundant natural resources, let’s unite to support inclusive and sustainable development. Together we can fight against gender-based violence! GBV is a crisis needing your urgent attention!  #NoExcuse

Chief Sunny Onuesoke, an environmentalist and managing partner of Das Energy Services Ltd, has urged the Federal Government to cease from undermining local experts, saying local engieers and other experts have the capacity to do jobs hitherto given to expatriates.
The former governorship aspirants in Delta State was speaking on the backdrop of Nigeria’s continued struggle with challenges of fuel importation and its impact on the economy.
While in a chat with the media recently, he said it was baffling that the nation’s refineries remained dormant despite decades of promises and billions of naira reportedly spent on Turn Around Maintenance (TAM), regretting that one such national asset is the Warri Refinery, a once-thriving industrial powerhouse located in the heart of Delta State.
He regretted the continued outsourcing of refinery rehabilitation to foreign companies, explaining that it is not only a wasteful practice but also a vote of no confidence in Nigerian engineers and companies.
He said; “Warri Refinery can be revived by competent engineering companies right here in Warri.I say this not as a sentiment but as a fact rooted in decades of experience,” he enthused.
“Warri is home to some of the most seasoned engineers, technicians and oil servicing firms in the entire West African region.
“These professionals have served with distinction in multinationals like Shell, Chevron and Nigerian Petroleum Development Company (NPDC). They are familiar with the terrain, the technology, and more importantly, the culture of the refinery itself.”
He continued; “Why then do we constantly overlook these homegrown professionals in favour of foreign companies who neither understand our local context nor offer long-term value beyond expensive consultancy fees?
“Let’s be clear; this isn’t just about national pride. It’s about economic sense, local content development, and national security.”
Chief Onuesoke called on the Federal Government to save the nation of huge foreign exchange by engaging Nigerian engineers to fix the facility, noting that with such, the FG would save the country millions in foreign exchange; empower our local economy; create jobs for the unemployed youths, and  builds technical self-reliance.
The Federal Government, he said, must break this cycle of dependency and stop the systemic sabotage of local talent.
“If a local firm can build modular refineries in Nigeria with private capital and no foreign aid, why should the same government claim that only foreign firms can fix existing state-owned refineries?
“We cannot continue this pattern of colonial industrial thinking — where every technical problem must have a foreign solution. It is time to trust Nigerian engineers, particularly those in Warri and the Niger Delta region who have devoted their lives to the oil and gas sector.
“I call on the Senate, the Federal Ministry of Petroleum, and the NNPC Ltd to urgently reassess their approach. Enough of international contracts that never yield results. Let us put faith in Nigerian hands to solve Nigerian problems.
“We can fix the Warri Refinery and we can do it with Warri-based engineers,” he concluded.
.

It has been well over a month since the law enforcement operation started in the Tigray region after the 4th of November 2020 attack and now the government has announced it has completed its military offence after taking the town of Mekele from the so called criminal group of Tigray People’s Liberation Front /TPLF/.
Although the government announced that the TPLF group had attacked the North National Defense, Sekoture Getachew, a veteran TPLF politician, publicly justified the November 4th military attack against the Northern Command of the Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF) as an anticipatory self-defense and amongst it all the international community still continues to force the Ethiopian government to accept independent investigation.
On Tuesday December 8, Redwan Hussein, spokesperson of the state of emergency told reporters that Ethiopia will invite others for assistance only if it feels that it failed to investigate.
“Ethiopia is led by a government which knows how to govern a nation. Ethiopia doesn’t need a baby sitter,” said Redwan.
Redwan confirmed that Ethiopia’s security forces shot to the air and detained United Nations staffers as they tried to reach parts of the embattled Tigray region that they were not supposed to go.
“They broke two checkpoints to drive hastily to areas where they were not supposed to go, that they were told not to go,” Ethiopian government spokesman Redwan Hussein said in a press conference.
“They were told in some areas they were not supposed to move. And when they were left alone they broke two checkpoints, and when they were about to break the third one, soliders shot to the air and detained them. Now, of course they are free,” Redwan explained.
Ethiopia’s government is making it clear it intends to manage the flow of humanitarian aid, but the U.N. has openly sought unfettered and neutral access according to international principles.
The U.N. announced deal with the Ethiopian government, saying it was signed on November 29. Crucially, the deal allows aid only in areas under Ethiopian government control. The government on Tuesday said 44 truckloads of food aid had been delivered to Shire, the main town near the refugee camps.
On Tuesday, Redwan repeated that message and added, “No entity, multilateral or unilateral, is supposed to supplant the government. We, the government, would call the shots.”
“Humanitarian assistance must be escorted by defense forces,” he said.
“The government will give allowance on where to go and where not to go. There are some forces who have not surrendered. They may not have some regular leadership and command and supply of resources but they can still keep on shooting until they run out of their arms. Thus, we are saying our humanitarian assistance has to be escorted with the military,” emphasized Redwan.
“Just because we completed the operation in three weeks it doesn’t mean we are in a picnic it was a very tough assignment it was completed successfully because the government was very much conscious about its people. Any life that dies during the operation is a lose to Ethiopia, but we are not hiding anybody killed by the government defense but because there was none there is no one to be accountable other than Ethiopians. It doesn’t matter if they were killed by government force or TIgray forces all are Ethiopians, we are not fighting with a foreign enemy it was a family feud,”Redwan stated vividly.
Regarding the humanitarian assistance, Mitiku Kassa, Commissioner of the National Risk and Disaster Management, said the commission is working to address humanitarian assistance to 1.8 million people in the region. However with the fear of the number increasing, the commission is working to do rapid assessment to capture additional number of beneficiaries, since between 22-30 percent of the urban population may need relief assistance for the short period of time.

By Abiy Ahmed
When I took office as Prime Minister of Ethiopia in April 2018, I had only one driving mission for my premiership – to put my country and people on a path to lasting peace and prosperity. I vowed to myself, my family and my people, in private and in public, that I would never resort to force as a way of resolving internal political differences. I believe that no problem is worthy of any bloodshed, that all problems can be resolved amicably if we have the courage of our convictions to sit around a table, in good faith, in search of mutually acceptable solutions. I further declared that the only enemy I would mobilize my people and resources to wage war against was poverty.
However, my vision and determination came under severe strain right from the start of my premiership. It did not take long for the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) leadership to launch a campaign, covertly and overtly, to undermine my administration and make our people and the rest of the world believe that, without them at the helm, Ethiopia would be ungovernable. To make their case, the TPLF leadership had to produce the evidence of ungovernability themselves, organizing a clandestine nationwide campaign of criminality and violence: sponsoring, financing, and training disaffected individuals to instigate communal clashes and attacks on members of ethnic minorities in different parts of the country. Attacks sponsored and orchestrated by the TPLF leadership left more than two million people internally displaced and thousands dead in the past two and half years.
I was fully aware that the TPLF leadership orchestrated the mayhem, bordering on party-sponsored terrorism, diverting budgetary resources allocated by the Federal Government to pay for their criminal enterprise and destabilize the nation. But, despite overwhelming pressure from the public for the Government to stop them by all means necessary, including through the use of force, I made it clear, repeatedly, that my Government would never resort to force to resolve the matter. I shared this firm and clear position to the TPLF leaders directly, in person and on the phone, and reassured the Ethiopian people, including our citizens in the Tigray Region, through mainstream and social media.
When the TPLF leadership rejected my personal invitations to engage with my administration in constructive dialogue on the future of our nation, I encouraged the country’s most senior religious and community leaders to travel to Mekelle, the capital of the Tigray Region, and help federal and regional political leaders resolve the differences peacefully. Regrettably, these most revered community and religious leaders were rebuffed by the TPLF leadership, treating them with utmost contempt and sending them back with nothing.
Even then, I did not give up; I would not. As I’ve said before, my own life has taught me that war is “the epitome of hell for all involved”. I did not come to office to take my people to hell; on the contrary, I came to office with a commitment to lead my people towards peace and prosperity. Since I came to office just over 30 months ago, I reiterated, time and again, that nothing would distract me away from my firm position on this matter. Regrettably, all my persistent efforts to avoid conflict by all means were taken for weakness.
In the end, however, the choice was not to be mine. While I was preaching peace and prosperity for my country and people, and working day and night to realize it, a violent attack was launched against my Government and people. On the night of 03 November 2020, the TPLF leadership launched, under cover of darkness, what they later described, on public television, as a “lightening pre-emptive attack” against the Northern Command of the Ethiopian National Defence Force (ENDF), which had been stationed in the Region since the outbreak of war with Eritrea over two decades ago. Using traitors recruited from within the army along ethnic lines, not only did the TPLF leadership cause the massacre of unarmed soldiers in their pyjamas in the dead of night, they also took possession, illegally, of the entire military arsenal of the Northern Command. I was thus left with a decision only of how, not whether, to fight to defend the integrity of my country and restore the constitutional order.
More than the attack, what shocked me and my fellow Ethiopians to the core was the level of cruelty the TPLF leadership displayed in the conduct of their criminal operations. After they surprised and overpowered several regiments of the ENDF forces, the TPLF identified and separated hundreds of unarmed Ethiopian soldiers of non-Tigrayan origin, tied their hands and feet together, massacred them in cold blood, and left their bodies lying in open air. Never would I have imagined it humanly possible for any person to kill their fellow soldiers while asleep and record themselves singing and dancing on the bodies of their victims.
Following their surprise attack on their own unsuspecting fellow Ethiopians, it didn’t take long for the TPLF leadership to start celebrating and gloating in public about their prowess and invincibility in war and how they have now transformed themselves, overnight, into the largest fighting force in the entire Horn of Africa.
With the benefit of hindsight, the surprise attack by the TPLF forces had three interrelated objectives. First, by attacking the Northern Command, which accounted for the bulk of Ethiopia’s most experienced combat forces, they aimed to weaken the capability of the ENDF to safeguard the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the country. Second, by using ethnic Tigrayans members of the ENDF to carry out the attack on their comrades-in-arms from other ethnic groups, they aimed to divide and destroy whatever was left of the ENDF as a cohesive national defence force. Third, once the ENDF was so fractured, defeated and destroyed, and the country almost certainly descended into anarchy, the TPLF would present themselves as the only force that could put the country back together, thus removing and replacing the federal government by force.
My primary duty as prime minister and commander in chief is to protect the nation and its people from internal and external enemies. That is why the Federal Government launched and successfully executed defensive operations to restore law and order in the Tigray Region, regrettably making the use of force the only tool left in our arsenal.
I recognize that, in the end, everyone is entitled to their opinions. Only history will judge whether the Federal Government under my leadership could have done anything else to resolve the existential crisis my old and proud nation faced on that fateful night of 03 November and its aftermath.
As I write this article, the Ethiopian army has completed its mission according to plan and captured the regional capital of Mekelle without the large-scale civilian casualties and war crimes that so many in the international community confidently predicted. Yet, despite the success of these operations, I’m not celebrating; I cannot be. While I admire the courage and sacrifice of our men and women in uniforms, I know the conflict has caused unimaginable suffering. This is a conflict in which Ethiopians had to kill their fellow Ethiopians, target and destroy their own defence infrastructure and weaken their own defence capability. At the same time, I also know that the Federal Government was forced to engage in this operation for existential reasons – the future of Ethiopia as a sovereign nation and the peaceful co-existence of its people was at stake. The heavy cost we incurred as a nation was necessary.
Now that the active phase of military operations is over, our next task is to launch the process of healing from the aftereffects of this traumatic conflict, to ensure our citizens in the affected areas, including those who have been forced to cross the borders to the Sudan, have unfettered access to humanitarian assistance and other support necessary to rehabilitate them back to normal life at the earliest opportunity. Also critical is the need to restore the transport and communications links destroyed by the conflict.
Having witnessed afresh the courage and determination of the Ethiopian people to protect their country from its enemies, I am confident that Ethiopia will rise back to its traditional role as the anchor of stability for the entire subregion and beyond.
At the same time, the peace and security we have restored at so much cost remain fragile. That is why we are determined to ensure our next elections, scheduled to take place in mid-2021, are fair, free, and inclusive, and that the people of Tigray, like all other Ethiopians, shall soon be led by a regional government of their free own choice.
